summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Aurelia through an edge-case playbook demonstrating long-context sessions (~100k tokens), sustained high-TPS bursts, and streaming backpressure handling. Key asks: run a daytime 24h pilot, share logs and traffic shapes, confirm security/KMS fit. Customer worried about tail latency, token-cost during long-running sessions, and private deployment constraints.
topics: Agenda: intro and goals (5m), reproduce Aurelia workload in Redwood console (15m), long-context KV/prefix caching demo (12m), simulated sustained 1k TPS burst & backpressure play (18m), failover/timeout policies and security/Q&A (12m)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Lena (Aurelia): Lena here, Marco, Priya, Oliver on.
[00:00:12] Diego (Redwood SE): Hey all, Diego from Redwood. We'll try to keep this practical — demo, then reproducer, then playbook.
[00:00:28] Samira: High level goal from your notes was: long-lived conversation windows for clinical summarization plus spikes of inference during daytime — is that still right?
[00:00:36] Marco (Platform): Yep. We're seeing sessions that keep growing, sometimes 40–80k tokens over weeks, and then we get these concentrated bursts when multiple doctors trigger batch exports.
[00:00:48] Priya (SRE): And our major concern is tail latency for interactive UX, plus unexpected costs from keeping kv cache live for huge sessions.
[00:01:02] Samira: Totally. We'll show three layers — runtime handling of long KV state, autoscale and queueing for TPS surges, and streaming backpressure & timeouts with graceful fallbacks.
[00:01:18] Diego: Jumping in — I'll start in the Console. (unintelligible) sorry, my screen share is poping — ok pulled up Aurelia demo workspace.
[00:01:34] [00:01:34] Diego: Here is our model route configured for conversation-long-state. Note the KV cache ttl is set to 72h for demo, kv eviction policy LRU but we can set weighted eviction per session.
[00:01:50] Marco: Can you spell kv? sometimes docs call it kv cache, kv-store — we've seen K-V cash in some logs.
[00:01:56] Diego: Yeah that's one of the transcription quirks — it's KV cache, short for key-value cache for the attention / prefix.
[00:02:08] Diego: I'll kick off a long-context replay — feeding a session that ramps to 90k tokens. You'll see the runtime stream in the console and the memory / cache metrics on the right.
[00:02:22] [00:02:22] Diego: 00:02:22 start replay; note here the runtime is doing continuous batching, the sequence length histogram is skewed right.
[00:02:34] Priya: Are you simulating multiple concurrent sessions or one big session?
[00:02:38] Diego: Single very long session first — then we'll spawn 400 concurrent short sessions to stress tps.
[00:02:46] [00:02:46] Diego: At ~00:04:30 you'll see an increase in kv-get rate and a spike in cache eviction. The console annotates evictions as 'session-evict'.
[00:03:02] Marco: I like that annotation. In our logs we often have 100s of tiny evictions that correlate to latency blips.
[00:03:12] Diego: Right, we also surface prefix hit-rate and per-token cost estimate. This helps you decide between longer TTL vs recompute.
[00:03:26] Samira: Quick note — the Optimize tab will show cost delta if you drop TTL to 24h and enable 4-bit quantization for that model family.
[00:03:36] Priya: Are those quant gains safe for clinical summarization? We can't degrade recall.
[00:03:42] Diego: Good question — Optimize ties into evals. We ran your sample prompt set with q4_0 and saw negligible ROUGE/recall drift on summaries, but we recommend a canary rollout.
[00:03:56] [00:03:56] Lena: Show us the canary config — how do you fallback if quality drops during pilot?
[00:04:02] Diego: In the rollout policy you set guardrails: 95p latency, and quality threshold on prompt set. If quality dips the router will fallback to the verified full-precision variant automatically.
[00:04:16] [00:04:16] Marco: Ok can we jump to the sustained TPS test?
[00:04:20] Diego: Yep — starting sustained burst sim: 1k TPS for 10 minutes, plus a tail of background long sessions. Starting now.
[00:04:30] [00:04:30] Diego: We intentionally bring the pool to a near-saturation point. Notice the queuing metric 'inflight-queue-length' rises while token latency stays within SLO for 95p due to batching.
[00:04:46] Priya: But the 99p seems to spike — what's the mitigation there?
[00:04:50] Diego: We have a few levers: dynamic priority routing, preemptible burst nodes, and a graceful degrade policy which responds with a short-form summary or reduced context when tail latency crosses threshold.
[00:05:06] [00:05:06] Marco: If we reduce context size as a fallback, how do we avoid hallucination risk?
[00:05:12] Diego: Fall back to structured templates and constrained decoding; we also keep important clinical anchors pinned in the prefix so key facts are preserved. It is a tradeoff but better than timeouts.
[00:05:30] Samira: Also note you can configure per-customer route policies — i.e., high-priority interactive clinicians vs batch jobs.
[00:05:40] [00:05:40] Lena: Security — last time you mentioned private control plane. Can we run this as private deployment with our KMS/HSM?
[00:05:48] Samira: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM, and we can integrate with your vault. For audit, we stream fine-grained logs to your SIEM.
[00:06:02] Priya: What about data residency? Some patient notes must stay in EU regions.
[00:06:08] Samira: You can pin routes to regions and the routing policy will never egress. We also do region-aware fallback so the system won't failover to a different residency unless explicitly allowed.
[00:06:22] [00:06:22] Marco: Back to the demo, I'm seeing occasional 'stream reset' events in the console under streaming-backpressure.
[00:06:28] Diego: That's intentionally injected. When a backend goes beyond soft ttl, the proxy will reset the stream and the client receives a retry token. The SDK will re-open as resumable chunk, not a fresh session.
[00:06:44] Marco: Does that mean the KV cache might be inconsistent between retries?
[00:06:48] Diego: We persist the prefix checkpoints. On retry the runtime does a diff and rehydrate up to a safe boundary. Sometimes transcriptions show 'k-v cash mismatch' because of mislabeling but the mechanism is robust.
[00:07:06] [00:07:06] Priya: For our SLOs we need 200ms median and 500ms 95p interactive — are those achievable under your demo config?
[00:07:14] Diego: Median yes on typical clinician prompts; 95p depends on session size and burstiness. Our console's simulated 1k TPS test had 95p ~420ms with batching windows tuned.
[00:07:28] Samira: We'll provide a tuned suggestion based on your actual traffic shape as a follow-up.
[00:07:36] [00:07:36] Diego: Now I'll pivot to a timeout/fallback play: I'll trigger an artificial network stall at the edge and show how the system produces an 'interim response' with a TTL-aware truncation.
[00:07:50] [00:07:50] Diego: Triggering stall... you'll see an interim chunk that says 'partial result — please retry for full detail', and downstream logs show the request reclassed as 'degraded-response'.
[00:08:06] Oliver (Product): From product lens that's good — but can customers override the interim messaging? We want consistent UX in the app.
[00:08:12] Samira: Yes, the SDK has localized strings and a hook for intercepting degraded responses so you can show your own UI treatment.
[00:08:22] [00:08:22] Marco: About cost — when you keep large prefixes and the session is long, we pay per token stored? or compute per rewind?
[00:08:30] Diego: Pricing combines per-token inference plus an optional long-state storage cost if you choose persistent prefix storage in Dedicated. Optimize shows estimates; we ran your sample and projected a 7–12% cost increase for 72h TTL vs 24h TTL.
[00:08:50] Priya: That delta is nontrivial over millions of sessions. Could caching be tiered so older parts are compressed?
[00:08:58] Diego: Yes, we have configurable archival quantization — older history can be quantized more aggressively and stored as compressed summaries rather than full KV. That reduces storage cost and still provides context anchors.
[00:09:12] [00:09:12] Lena: For the pilot — can you ingest our protobuf event stream directly for 24h?
[00:09:18] Diego: We prefer a sanitized replay, but we can stream live with a staging token. We'll need a sample mapping to our ingestion schema, and we'll mask PHI per your policy.
[00:09:30] [00:09:30] Diego: Starting the 400-concurrent short sessions now to show mixing workload.
[00:09:42] [00:09:42] Diego: Notice now the system prioritizes interactive routes and pushes batch jobs to lower priority fleet. You can tune preempt policy to prefer clinicians.
[00:09:56] Marco: When preempting, do you guarantee batch jobs won't be killed mid-request?
[00:10:02] Diego: We try to drain them gracefully; if it's critical we support canary routing with dedicated nodes per tenant to avoid preemption.
[00:10:12] [00:10:12] Priya: How do you handle long-lived WebSocket connections and connection churn during spikes? We saw connection resets in test.
[00:10:20] Diego: The proxy uses a keepalive buffer and resumable streaming tokens so the SDK can resume from last acked chunk. There's a sliding window to avoid re-computing full prefix.
[00:10:34] [00:10:34] Marco: Any caveats with TLS session renegotiation and HSM integration?
[00:10:40] Samira: For Private we support mutual TLS and integrate with most HSMs we tested. There is a small perf hit on initial handshake, but steady-state is fine. We'll share the HSM compatibility matrix.
[00:10:54] [00:10:54] Oliver: Who owns the fallback logic in an on-prem install?
[00:10:58] Diego: You own the control plane when on-prem, but our agent implements the runtime and policies. We ship the policy templates and rarely customers need to modify low-level code.
[00:11:12] [00:11:12] Samira: Quick poll — does the architecture look like it would meet your compliance and latency needs?
[00:11:20] Lena: Mostly yes. We need to validate that fallback summaries don't leak PHI and that log streams are scrubbed.
[00:11:28] Priya: Also want proof that KMS keys never leave our tenancy.
[00:11:32] Samira: Understood — action: we'll send SOC2/ISO pack and an HSM attestation note.
[00:11:42] [00:11:42] Diego: Final part — resilience play: simulate a regional node failure and show automatic fallback to a warm replica with degraded throughput but preserved session continuity.
[00:11:56] [00:11:56] Diego: Simulating regional failover... you can see the connection stays alive, 'replica-sync' logs show delta rehydrate. Throughput dips, but no hard timeouts.
[00:12:10] Marco: That's compelling. But what's the RTO for the replica rehydrate for 80k token sessions?
[00:12:16] Diego: Typical rehydrate to safe boundary is 6–18s depending on network; full rehydrate for the entire prefix is longer but we keep checkpoints for critical anchors to allow continued operation.
[00:12:30] [00:12:30] Lena: Ok let's talk deliverables.
[00:12:34] Samira: We'll: 1) run a 24h replay/pilot; 2) provide a tuned TTL/quant suggestion; 3) share security/compliance docs; 4) price the Dedicated option and a mixed hosted model.
[00:12:46] [00:12:46] Marco: Good. Do you have a sample SLO contract?
[00:12:50] Samira: Yes — we'll attach a starter SLO template with 95/99 latency targets and escalation paths.
[00:12:58] Priya: One last question — how does the SDK surface degraded-response to the app? Is it an error code?
[00:13:04] Diego: It's an extended response envelope: status=degraded, reason=timeout/fallback, retry_token. SDK interceptors can map that to UI states.
[00:13:18] [00:13:18] Lena: Great demo. We'll assign internal owners and get you the staging access.
[00:13:24] Samira: Thanks — we'll follow up with the pilot plan.
[00:13:28] [00:13:28] Recording Bot: Transcription auto-chunks end. Note: some technical terms may be mis-transcribed (k-v, h s m, etc).
notes: Customer emphasized PHI scrubbing and KMS tenancy. AE recommended a staged pilot. SE suggested compressing old history and pinned anchors to reduce hallucination. Security asks: SOC2, HSM attestation, log-scrubbing proof. Pricing: estimate follow-up for Dedicated vs mixed-hosted.
